test.name: An arrival a project record shows to be a return trip does not make a naturalization interval a shortfall
test.description: The counterpart to ut_person_evidence_n5r: the same June 1871 arrival and 13 Aug 1875 naturalization, but I1 is already linked to an 1869 San Francisco directory entry at 5 Cook, the register's address, so he was resident before the arrival, the 1871 arrival is a return trip, and residence from 1869 clears the five years. The agent must not flag the interval as an unexplained shortfall or put it in a core_identifier_conflict. The directory record is synthetic (see the scenario README). Issue #3969.

input.delegation:
Question: q_001 (when and from where in Germany did Hermann Gaetjen immigrate; tree I1 Hermann, husband of I4 Amelia Nichols, father of I2 Henry Joseph b. 5 May 1878 San Francisco and I3 Amelia Otillie b. 23 Aug 1883 California).
Link these to the right person in the tree:
- src_001, assertions a_001 to a_009: 1875 San Francisco Great Register, Hermann Gatjen, 21, b. Germany, fireman, 5 Cook Street, naturalized 13 Aug 1875, California 4th District Court.
- src_002, assertions a_010 to a_014: Germans to America Index, Herm Gaetjen, b. 1854 Prussia, arrived New York 2 Jun 1871.
Already linked to I1: src_003 (a_015, a_016), the 1869 San Francisco directory.
Decide identity yourself with same_person scoring. I1's only birth fact (about 1859) is unsourced. If the evidence does not support linking either persona to I1, put it on a separate stub and say so.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: I1 is linked at `probable` (pe_001, pe_002) to src_003, an 1869 San Francisco directory entry, "Gaetjen Hermann, apprentice, 5 Cook", and carries the residence as F3. The 1875 register gives the same 5 Cook address. He was therefore resident in San Francisco before the 2 June 1871 New York arrival, so that arrival is a return trip, not his first entry, and residence from 1869 to 13 August 1875 exceeds the five years the 1802 act required.

Decided rule (lead, 2026-11-01): only an unexplained arrival-to-naturalization shortfall caps the links at `probable` and is named. A shortfall that a project record explains takes the ordinary tiers. Naming the interval and then the return trip that explains it is good reasoning and is credited. Stating an unexplained shortfall, capping or lowering a link because of the interval, or a `core_identifier_conflict` about it, is the rule over-firing: a partial on Confidence calibration, and a FAIL on Rationale quality if the rationale presents the interval as unexplained.

A Naturalization check line that counts the residence from the 1869 directory and reports the five years met is the return trip stated another way: it is correct reasoning and passes Rationale quality. So is putting the 1871 arrival on a stub and writing no check line for it, since the arrival is then not on I1.

Stubbing the arrival, or declining to link it, because the 1869 residence and the 1871 arrival are treated as mutually exclusive (an impossibility, two places at once, different men, or a return trip ruled out) is also the failure this test guards, whatever the tier: a FAIL on Rationale quality. Read the stub's rationale, or the reply when no entry is written. Stubbing it on its 0.006 score alone is not.

A Naturalization check line reading "4 years 2 months vs required 5 years: met" followed by the 1869 directory (src_003, pe_001 or pe_002) is CORRECT, not a factual error: the five years are counted from the 1869 residence, not from the 1871 arrival, so the requirement is met. Do not mark it down on any dimension.

same_person scores the register persona 0.43 (confidence 3) and finds no match for the arrival (0.006). Identity otherwise rests on name, approximate age and city, so `probable` is the ordinary tier for the register, and the arrival may be linked `speculative` or put on a stub on its weak score. Those tiers come from the match strength and are not the interval rule over-firing.
The birth year in both records (1854) differs from I1's unsourced about 1859 by five years. That is a separate question from the interval and is not marked either way here.

GROUNDING: decide what the run DID from its written person_evidence entries. A rationale on a_007 or a_014 that states a shortfall without the return trip, or a `core_identifier_conflict` on either about the interval, is the failure this test guards.
